items: **Existing thread:** Christopher replied to Tunahan on LinkedIn, said he would reach out if priorities change, and sent his work email — Tunahan is the warmest sender.

**Computational biology:** Tunahan (CSO, 20+ years in RNA analysis; systems biology and transcriptomics at Gebze Technical University) speaks directly to the "AI and computational biology" area B+L named in August 2026.

**Scientific innovation role:** Christopher's title points to scouting outside science; Saliha (CEO, PhD, 15+ years in bioinformatics) leads PhiTech's biopharma offer (molecular profiling, data & AI, trial stratification).
No shared employer, school, co-author or event was found for Saliha or Tunahan and Christopher. His career history could not be verified on the public web.

lead_with.title: Respect his "no", ask one question
lead_with.text: He said rare-disease precision medicine is not a core focus. Do not pitch again. Ask what B+L's **AI and computational biology** effort is looking for, and whether multi-omics (DNA + RNA) analysis has a place in it.

lead_with.title: Retina is the only clinical bridge
lead_with.text: B+L is building in **retinal disease** (geographic atrophy: RNAi deal with City Therapeutics, sustained-release implant from Whitecap). PhiTech's offer for biopharma — **molecular profiling, biomarkers, patient stratification** — is the angle, not diagnostics.

lead_with.title: Keep it a low-cost door
lead_with.text: Offer a short note or a 20-minute exchange between Tunahan and his team on RNA-based analysis — a scientist-to-scientist talk, not a sales demo. Then let it rest until he signals interest.

company.text: Bausch + Lomb is a global eye-health company (founded 1853) selling contact lenses, lens care, consumer eye care (LUMIFY, Artelac), ophthalmic pharmaceuticals (MIEBO, Xiidra) and surgical products (premium IOLs, glaucoma devices). It reports three segments: Vision Care, Surgical and Pharmaceuticals. Bausch Health owns about **87%** of its shares and plans to separate it, through a share distribution, a sale or another transaction. On Oct 12, 2026 CEO Brent Saunders left by mutual agreement; **Thomas J. Appio**, CEO of Bausch Health, is now chairman and interim CEO. In August 2026 B+L said its pipeline spans dry eye, surgical, consumer, contact lenses, retinal diseases and "emerging areas including **AI and computational biology**". In July 2026 it stopped a glaucoma neuroprotection program after a failed Phase 2 and refocused that asset on geographic atrophy.

financials.text: **Q3 2026 (reported Oct 28, 2026):** revenue US$1.375B (+7% reported, +8% constant currency); Vision Care US$774M, Surgical US$234M, Pharmaceuticals US$367M. **GAAP net income** US$32M (vs loss of US$28M). **Adjusted EBITDA** US$325M. **Cash flow from operations** US$233M. **R&D** US$91M in the quarter. **2026 guidance raised:** revenue US$5.45–5.55B; adjusted EBITDA (excl. acquired IPR&D) US$1.09–1.14B. **Cash** US$515M; long-term debt about US$5.05B (Sep 30, 2026). Owner: Bausch Health (~87%). Spending is focused on brands that grow (MIEBO +42%, LUMIFY +35%, premium IOLs ~+70%) — a small external data partnership would sit in R&D or innovation budgets, not commercial ones.

talking_points: You said rare-disease precision medicine isn't a core focus — has anything changed since June, especially with the new leadership?
B+L now lists AI and computational biology as an emerging area: what kind of problems is that team trying to solve?
In retina and geographic atrophy, do your programs use genomic or RNA data for biomarkers or patient selection?
Who inside B+L owns external partnerships for data and AI tools — your team, R&D, or clinical development?
Would a short scientist-to-scientist exchange with Tunahan on RNA-based analysis be useful, with no commitment?
